evals.prompt: sync my branch, I need to pull in the latest from origin and push my stuff back up
evals.expected_output: Performs full sync cycle: fetches from origin, rebases onto upstream, confirms with user before pushing, then pushes. Reports fetch/rebase/push results.
expectations: fetches latest refs from origin
rebases the current branch onto the upstream tracking branch
confirms with the user before pushing
pushes the rebased branch to remote after confirmation
reports the full sync result: commits fetched, rebased, and pushed

evals.prompt: fetch rebase and push, I want my branch fully synced with remote
evals.expected_output: Recognizes the three-step workflow as a sync intent. Fetches, rebases, and pushes in sequence. Does NOT use --force; uses standard push.
expectations: recognizes 'fetch rebase and push' as a sync intent
performs fetch, rebase, and push in sequence
does NOT create merge commits during rebase
asks for push confirmation before pushing
does NOT use --force push

evals.expected_output: Uses 'upstream' as the remote and 'develop' as the target. Fetches from upstream, rebases onto upstream/develop, confirms, then pushes.
expectations: uses 'upstream' as the remote instead of origin
targets 'develop' as the branch to sync against
fetches from upstream and rebases onto upstream/develop
pushes to the correct remote after confirmation

evals.prompt: sync my branch with main, I think the push might need a force since I rebased earlier
evals.expected_output: Completes fetch and rebase. Shows what will be pushed. Confirms with user before pushing. Does NOT use --force unless user explicitly confirms.
expectations: completes fetch and rebase steps first
shows commits that will be pushed via git log
confirms with the user before pushing
does NOT use --force unless the user explicitly requests it
suggests re-running /sync if push is rejected

evals.prompt: sync up my feature/billing branch, I have uncommitted changes in the invoice template though
evals.expected_output: Detects dirty working directory. Offers stash/abort/proceed options. If stashing, performs sync then pops stash after.
expectations: detects uncommitted changes via git status --porcelain
offers three options: stash and sync, abort, or proceed with dirty tree
waits for user choice before continuing
if stashing, pops the stash after successful sync
does NOT silently discard uncommitted work

evals.prompt: sync my branch to latest, there will probably be conflicts in the database migration files
evals.expected_output: Fetches and begins rebase. If conflicts occur, halts the sync pipeline, does NOT push, and provides conflict resolution guidance.
expectations: fetches and begins the rebase operation
halts the sync pipeline if rebase conflicts occur
does NOT push if the rebase was not completed cleanly
provides conflict resolution guidance with git rebase --continue and --abort
shows the conflicted files

evals.prompt: sync everything with remote, I think I'm already up to date but I have 2 local commits to push
evals.expected_output: Fetches and detects no new upstream changes. Skips unnecessary rebase. Shows 2 local commits to push, confirms, then pushes them.
expectations: fetches and detects no new upstream changes to rebase
skips unnecessary rebase when already up to date
shows the 2 local commits that will be pushed
asks for confirmation before pushing
reports current sync status with pushed commit count

evals.prompt: hey can you sync my branch? I need to pull latest from origin/main and then push so the CI pipeline runs against my updated code
evals.expected_output: Full sync cycle targeting origin/main. Fetches, rebases onto origin/main, confirms push, pushes. Reports everything so user knows CI will see the update.
expectations: fetches from origin
rebases onto origin/main
confirms before pushing
pushes to remote so CI can run
reports success with commit details
